verdict.zero_error_tail (primary): ALIVE if Z <= 0.10 and Wilson hi <= 0.20 and n_long >= 30; WEAK if Z <= 0.30; DEAD if Z > 0.30
verdict.reaction (secondary): ALIVE if effect CI lo >= 0.10; WEAK if effect CI lo > 0; DEAD otherwise
verdict.caps: aiv_cu: proxy -> both capped at WEAK; aiv_cc: single-agent case study; Gemini: verdict from the union indicator, labelled 'union of two unvalidated-together classes'
verdict.threshold_reason: judgment calls fixed here. Context from A (not an outcome of this probe): per-call native error rates were 614/13,592 (swechat CC), 349/5,164 (cc_local), 538/33,475 (aiv_cc); at the L75 call counts in resolved.probe3 an independent-error model predicts almost no zero-error long sessions, so Z mostly measures how clumped errors are across sessions.

min_n.retry_verdict: >= 30 failed c_i with a successor from >= 10 sessions, and >= 30 non-failed c_i

early_late.eligible: sessions with n_calls >= 20 (>= 10 calls per half)
early_late.split: calls ordered by seq (all threads); early = first floor(n/2), late = the rest
early_late.statistic: late rate - early rate (sum errors / sum calls per half over sessions), statistic_ci with paired session resampling; also the share of sessions with errors early but none late (Wilson)
early_late.label: descriptive only (no verdict); 'stable' if the difference CI contains 0

retry.pair: consecutive calls (c_i, c_{i+1}) of the same thread by seq, where c_i has a paired result
retry.similarity: Jaccard of the token sets (sim_token, lowercased) of c_i and c_{i+1}: the shell command for shell tools, otherwise all string/number values of the parsed args
retry.retry: c_{i+1} has the same tool_key AND (identical args OR Jaccard >= 0.5); 'exact' if identical args
retry.classes_apart: c_i with cc_permission_denied / cc_interrupt_reject results are reported as their own rows
retry.similarity_reason: 0.5 = at least half of the distinct tokens shared; a judgment call fixed here. No A retry rate was computed.

deviations.why: the Phase B task specification for this probe names analysis/out/probe_3.json; the content contract (raw counts, prereg.json sha256 copied in, verdicts under `verdicts`) is kept

deviations.item: Gemini per-call error rate vs E0
deviations.prereg_said: error_definitions.swechat/gemini: two classes never pooled into one rate, union used only as a session indicator; probe3.zero_error_tail: E0 uses p = the unit's pooled B per-call primary error rate
deviations.what_you_did: per-call rates reported per class; the union per-call rate is reported once, labelled, and used only as p in E0 (and in the early/late union row, labelled)
deviations.why: E0 needs a per-call p for the indicator that decides the verdict (union); no other way to apply both clauses
deviations.effect_on_verdict: none (E0 is reported, not part of the verdict rule)

deviations.prereg_said: probe3.units.dead lists swechat/simple_text ('no calls'); PREREG.md section 0 says 0 B sessions -> NOT_TESTABLE in every probe
deviations.what_you_did: recorded DEAD as listed in prereg.json probe3.units.dead (JSON wins), with 0 B sessions noted
deviations.why: prereg.json is authoritative where the two differ

deviations.prereg_said: consecutive calls (c_i, c_{i+1}) of the same thread by seq, where c_i has a paired result
deviations.what_you_did: c_{i+1} ranges over all calls of the thread (deduplicated on (session_id, call_id), first by seq), paired or not; the A-split feasibility count in prereg_calibration.py used paired calls only. The number of pairs whose successor is unpaired is reported (retry.successor_pairs_next_unpaired)
deviations.why: literal reading of the SPEC text; the calibration count was a feasibility count, not a definition
deviations.effect_on_verdict: none expected (unpaired calls are a fraction of a percent; the count is reported)
